question.problem:
Which of the following augmented matrices are in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 9 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 & 7 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that an augmented matrix is in row echelon form if its coefficient matrix satisfies the following conditions:

I. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the bottom of the matrix.

II. Each leading entry of a row is in a column to the right of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 9 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is not in row echelon form since the second row contains only zeros and it is not at the bottom of the matrix (condition I is violated).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 7 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $A$ and $C$ are in row echelon form.
